review_candidates.title: Media Buyer / Creative Strategist (Remote)
review_candidates.description: Media buying is now the easy part. In 2026, the buying itself is piping. The levers that actually move a DTC account are creative, offer, and conversion rate, and the platform keeps getting better at rewarding whoever gets those right. So we don't hire media buyers. We hire marketers who buy media. At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands across our service lines, 20 to 25 of them on paid media, and we spend $6-9M a month on Meta. We're hiring one person to own a handful of those accounts end to end. Here's what "end to end" actually means here. You are the account manager. We don't have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership and accountability: when you're the person answering for the account, it's your result, not somebody else's summary of your result. You are the creative strategist. You do the research, you find the angles, and you write the briefs and the scripts. You direct our editors and designers rather than filing requests with them. Creative isn't a ticket you submit. It's your job. You build the things the account needs. If conversion rate is the bottleneck, you build the landing page. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme. You carry up to six accounts. That's the capacity we run at today, and the team averages about four and a half. You'll manage far fewer accounts than you would at most agencies. In exchange you get real ownership of the results and you get to work as an end to end marketer instead of one station on an assembly line. You can live anywhere. We're a remote team and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you're the client's point of contact and there's nobody else to cover it. The rest of your day is yours. If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we'll both know it fast. If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading. Requirements What the job looks like Own 4 to 6 DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, the creative lead, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $30k/mo to $1M/mo. Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you're the one who answers when something isn't working. Run the research before the ads. Marketing is 80% research here. You mine customer reviews, ad comments, support tickets, and Reddit for the language and objections that become angles. You pull competitor ad libraries. You run our internal tooling that OCRs and transcribes the ads in your account and ties them to performance, so you know what winning and losing actually look like in this account. Write the briefs and the scripts, and direct the work. Creative direction is yours. You run revision rounds with our editors and designers and you hold the quality bar. Ship creative on a cadence. Roughly 8 to 10 new ad launches a week is where accounts hold, in batches every 1 to 1.5 weeks. Informed volume, not spray and pray. We want better hypotheses, not more randomness. Build and test landing pages. Advertorials, comparison pages, PDPs. Built in Claude Code, deployed to Vercel, tested live on a subdomain before anything gets pushed into the client's theme. Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team. Report on new customer economics. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended ROAS and not last click. You'll be expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. You're a fit if You've done this with real money. Hands-on Meta at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. You're AI-native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude (or equivalent) as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it. If you can research, write, and build a converting page from scratch, we can teach you the buying. You can write direct response in English at a native or near-native level. Hooks, scripts, ad copy, advertorial. In the customer's own words, not invented. This is the single biggest source of leverage in the role and the thing we screen hardest for. If writing persuasive English isn't a strength, this isn't the job. You can communicate your ideas. This matters as much as anything else on this list. You'll be in front of clients constantly with nobody in between, so you need to be able to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. You have taste and you know when to hand off. You direct creative, you don't half-build it yourself. AI slop shipped to a client is a habit we break, not a shortcut we accept. You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you. Bonus: you've built or operated your own Shopify store or eComm brand. Several of our team have, and it shows. You're not a fit if "That wasn't my role" is in your vocabulary. It's the fastest way to end an interview here. If creative was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the creative You want to be told what to do this week You need a ticketing system to know what matters Benefits Why This Role Is Exciting This is not a maintenance job. You will be surrounded by people who move fast, care a lot, and take the work seriously. You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale. You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

review_candidates.title: MSCA Doctoral Researcher, DETECTIVE project (virology) / Väitöskirjatutkija (virologia)
review_candidates.description: Tampere University is a unique, boldly future‑oriented and evolving community, and one of Finland’s most multidisciplinary universities. At Tampere University, technology, health and society come together in a distinctive way. Our research groups and projects carry out interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral research that transcends organisational boundaries. Our community is international, with members from more than 80 countries. Read more at https://www.tuni.fi/en/tau. DETECTIVE (Data-driven Excellence in Training of Epidemiological, Clinical, Technological and Innovative Virus Experts) is a Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network. The network brings together leading academic, public health, clinical, and industrial partners across Europe to train the next generation of researchers in epidemic intelligence, emerging virus surveillance, and pandemic preparedness. Through interdisciplinary research and international collaboration, DETECTIVE aims to improve the early detection of emerging pathogens, strengthen risk assessment, and support real-time, evidence-based public health decision-making. Read more at virusdetective.eu Population dynamics and emerging epidemics Background of Project Doctoral Candidate 8 Enteroviruses are common human pathogens that cause infections ranging from asymptomatic or mild disease to severe neurological, cardiac and systemic illness. While some enterovirus types circulate continuously in the population, others show epidemic or re-emerging patterns and can cause large outbreaks. The factors determining when an enterovirus type shifts from limited circulation to epidemic spread remain incompletely understood. Population immunity is likely to play an important role in these dynamics. Type-specific neutralizing antibodies induced by previous infections can provide long-lasting protection, while susceptible individuals continuously enter the population. Consequently, immunity against individual enterovirus types changes across age groups, birth cohorts and calendar time, potentially creating population-level immunity gaps that favor epidemic emergence. This doctoral project will investigate how enterovirus circulation and population immunity have changed over time and whether these dynamics can be used to predict epidemic risk. The project will exploit the unique longitudinal resources of the Finnish DIPP study, which has collected biological samples from children since 1994, and integrate these data with healthcare surveillance, wastewater monitoring and historical epidemic data. The ultimate goal is to identify immunological and epidemiological signals associated with epidemic emergence and use them to develop predictive models for enterovirus epidemic risk. Job Description And Research Objectives At Tampere University, DETECTIVE is looking for a Doctoral Candidate 8 to work on Work Package 2. As Doctoral Candidate 8, you will: Characterize type-specific enterovirus immunity across age groups, birth cohorts and calendar periods using longitudinal serum samples and neutralizing antibody analyses. Investigate long-term enterovirus circulation in the background population and integrate these findings with healthcare surveillance and wastewater monitoring. Identify population susceptibility and immunity patterns associated with increased enterovirus circulation and epidemic emergence. Develop and validate predictive models for enterovirus epidemic risk by integrating longitudinal immunological, virological and surveillance data. Work with unique longitudinal sample collections and datasets spanning more than three decades and combine laboratory-based virology and serology with epidemiological data analysis and predictive modelling. The project will be carried out within a multidisciplinary and international research environment, with opportunities to collaborate with experts in virology, epidemiology, bioinformatics, public health and epidemic modelling across the DETECTIVE network. Supervisory Team The DC Will Be Supervised By Adj. Professor Sami Oikarinen Dr. Jutta Laiho Additional Scientific Mentoring And Collaboration Will Be Provided By Prof. Heikki Hyöty at Tampere University Dr. Sarah Kempster (MHRA) Prof. Nicholas Grassly (ICL) Planned Secondments The doctoral candidate will undertake international secondments within the DETECTIVE network, including: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA, UK) for training related to antibody standards Imperial College London (ICL, UK) for training in population immunity and epidemic-risk modelling These secondments will provide exposure to both academic and industrial research environments and offer opportunities to develop complementary scientific and transferable skills. Requirements We are looking for a motivated researcher with a relevant Master’s degree in biomedical sciences, bioinformatics, microbiology, virology, immunology, epidemiology, or a related field. Experience with molecular technologies and bioinformatics will be considered an advantage. The successful candidate should be highly motivated to develop expertise in data science, including machine learning and artificial intelligence, and to apply these approaches to biomedical and epidemiological data. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, an interest in self-development, and the ability to work in a multidisciplinary research environment are expected. In accordance with the MSCA mobility rule, applicants must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Finland for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding 1 March 2027. Compulsory national service and/or short stays such as holidays and time spent as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status under the Geneva Convention are not considered. An applicant must have completed a relevant Master’s degree before the starting date of employment. We offer We offer a three-year Doctoral Candidate position placed at Tampere University within the EU-funded MSCA Doctoral Network DETECTIVE. A trial period of six (6) months applies to all our new employees. The salary will be set in accordance with MSCA rates. Target degree is PhD degree from Tampere University, Finland. The doctoral researcher has the opportunity to work with unique longitudinal biological samples and epidemiological data from the Finnish DIPP study, covering more than three decades of enterovirus circulation. A multidisciplinary research project combining virology, immunology, epidemiology, population surveillance and predictive modelling. Access to the international DETECTIVE research and training network spanning academic institutions, public health organisations, regulatory bodies and industry. Interdisciplinary network-wide training schools (one week each): Foundations in Virology, Bioinformatics and Epidemiology; Advanced Integration of Scientific, Diagnostic and Public Health Virology Translational Virology and connecting Academia, Clinical Practice and Public Health for Pandemic Preparedness. An individually tailored career development plan and personal empowerment programme. Access to the Campus Sport Services at a personnel price. Tampere University offers a wide range of other staff benefits too, such as occupational health care, flexible working hours, and several restaurants and cafés on campus with staff discounts. Read more about working at Tampere University: https://www.tuni.fi/en/tau/work-with-us. Tampere University (TAU), founded in 1925, is an internationally oriented research university with a strong focus on multidisciplinary research and education at the intersection of technology, health, and society. With ten schools, approximately 23,200 students and 4,200 staff members, including around 330 professors, TAU is the second-largest university in Finland and provides a dynamic and international environment for high-quality research and doctoral education. Read more about Tampere University https://www.tuni.fi/en/tau/about-tampere-university and work in Tampere https://workintampere.fi/. TAU offers excellent research infrastructure for virology, metagenomics, and environmental research. The available facilities include a dedicated metagenomics core facility, an extensive environmental wastewater sample and data bank, Biosafety Level 2 and 3 laboratories, and dedicated clean areas for PCR and cell culture work. Researchers also have access to a broad range of university-wide core facilities and services through the TAU Met-Core Facilities and Services. The virology research environment is further supported by a large collection of wild-type enteroviruses isolated from different countries and continents.
